Title: BMW Program Manager
Description:
**Duties & Responsibilities**

**Client Partnership & Programme Governance**

* Act as direct support to the BMW ME Training Manager in planning, executing and controlling the Training Centre, its activities and resources.
* Act as GP Strategies' primary point of contact and escalation for BMW on the training programme.
* Develop and maintain programme and project plans, including milestones, owners, deliverables, budget, implementation timing and approval gateways, with a plan for each new learning initiative.
* Lead the start-up phase of new projects, including problem definition, concept development and vendor selection.
* Identify training and coaching opportunities that support BMW ME's business objectives, using requirements obtained from the market or the BMW Regional Office (RO). Evaluate the training strategy against changing market and importer needs, and recommend new learning and development initiatives to BMW.
* Lead the development of training and coaching programmes, with Trainer input, for BMW approval.
* Set up meetings, supported by the Training Co-ordinator, with the people responsible for each new project and for approving the proposed solution.
* Ensure each new programme is delivered on time, within budget and to BMW standards, including reporting and participant feedback.
* Set up and own the training materials repository, together with the Training Co-ordinator, tracking all existing material under version control so that there is a clean, current record of every update, replacement and enhancement; ensure materials developed for new programmes are provided to BMW and retained in the repository.
* Using the repository as the starting point for material reviews and overhauls, revisit existing training programmes so that they reflect the current product range and BMW's updated training methods; table update plans with BMW where needed, and execute them once approved.
* Receive the Sales & Product Trainers' proposals for improving sales training materials and methodologies, and decide which to take forward as part of programme reviews and overhauls.
* Review and approve the annual training plan and training calendar prepared by the Training Co-ordinator before submission to BMW.
* Support the training needs analysis.
* Support quarterly adjustments to the training plan.
* Support the planning of Focus Training and coaching.
* Manage programme risks, issues and changes, and communicate their impact on scope, timelines, resources and cost.
* Maintain programme documentation, decisions and action logs.
* Maintain a formal improvement tracker of all proposals tabled with BMW, together with BMW's responses.
* Record and track all new projects delivered by or via GP, and all value-added services.
* Lead GP's participation in audits, programme reviews and BMW governance activities.

**Client Meetings & Reporting**

* Run the weekly operations meeting with the team, covering priorities, delivery status and actions.
* Chair the monthly client meeting with BMW, covering performance, KPIs, SLA results and the forward plan.
* Lead the quarterly account meeting with BMW, including review of annual volumetrics, capacity assumptions and demand trends.
* Review all reports and the monthly KPI scoreboard before they are sent to BMW.
* Own and sign off the monthly SLA report, and chair the monthly joint review of the SLA exception register with BMW.
* Keep BMW and the BMW RO informed of successes and noteworthy stories, and maintain a success log with evidence.

**Financial Control**

* Prepare annual budget inputs, including training volumes, trainer mix and costs, for the Senior Director, who sets rates and agrees the budget with BMW.
* Control all programme financials against the approved budget, including spend, variance and BMW over- or under-spend, and escalate commercial risks.
* Prepare the monthly forward forecast of revenue, vendor cost and training volumes.
* Control GP revenue recovery: sign off monthly BMW invoicing so that all billable activity is recovered, and reconcile SLA credit deductions.
* Reconcile vendor costs against BMW invoicing every month.
* Support the maintenance of the training tracker and the monthly billing data.
* Liaise with GP Finance and the Senior Director on billing, forecasting and commercial matters.

**Service Quality, KPIs & SLA Compliance**

* Set, monitor and control KPIs for the entire team; act on deviations and identify improvement opportunities.
* Define, maintain and monitor service delivery quality standards for the Training Centre, and lead continuous-improvement reviews.
* Receive and review the Training Administrator's reports on the Operating Standards Manual and the adoption of agreed processes across the team, and act on any gaps.
* Submit Deviation Requests to BMW by the 14-day fill-rate measurement date.
* Submit Legitimate Cause claims with supporting evidence within the contractual timelines.
* Direct the Training Administrator's support in preparing Deviation Requests and Legitimate Cause claims.
* Dispute SLA results with evidence within 5 business days of notification.
* Issue Service Rectification Plans and corrective and preventive action plans when Non-Compliance Events occur.
* Hold accountability for the compliance register of vendor agreements, work permits, licences and sub-supplier documents maintained by the Training Administrator.

**Product Launches, Conferences & Events**

* Own all product launches, conferences and events end to end, as decision-maker and custodian of quality, budget, BMW CI and brand standards, approvals and execution, liaising with BMW so that decisions reflect its requirements.
* Review and approve launch event concepts developed by the Training Co-ordinator, together with BMW.
* Lead the briefing for each launch or event, and feed approved concepts and decisions through to the team and external event suppliers.
* Support the team in the operational delivery of launches and events, as briefed.

**Vendor Oversight**

* Approve training vendors and programmes together with BMW and the BMW regional office.
* Produce a briefing document for supplier tender, or for a selected supplier to GP, setting out the programme requirement, key success factors, budget and timing, and appoint the supplier.
* Hold an annual review with each supplier, including written feedback from importers, participants and BMW where possible.

**People & Resource Management**

* Lead the BMW ME team to achieve its KPIs and SLA obligations.
* Manage the performance of direct reports, including objectives, quarterly conversations, reviews and performance improvement plans.
* Manage time sheets and approve leave and sickness for all Training Centre staff, and handle team escalations.
* Act as the escalation point for internal operational matters handled day to day by the Training Co-ordinator.
* Manage grievances and employee issues together with GP Strategies management.
* Manage the performance of employed and vendor trainers against SLA quality and conduct requirements.
* Sit in on training regularly to ensure employed and vendor trainers maintain training standards consistently, and give them feedback.
* Recruit staff, including CV review, interviews and scoring.
* Maintain a recruitment pipeline and back-up resource plan, and fill replacement or additional roles within 3 months.
* Replace trainers within 5 business days when required by BMW, or put interim mitigation in place.
* Support trainer capacity planning and allocation.
* Onboard and certify new or replacement trainers.
* Support trainer calibration, train-the-trainer and professional development.
* Seek opportunities to reward and recognise the team and vendor trainers.

**Ad Hoc Duties**

* Undertake additional duties associated with the successful delivery of the BMW ME training programme, as reasonably required by the Senior Director.

**Key Performance Measures**

The Programme / Project Manager is measured on the performance of the programme as a whole, including the SLA requirements in the BMW contract addendum effective 1 January 2027:

* Course fill-rate of at least 95% (minimum 8 participants where applicable) and delivery of the agreed annual training volume.
* Participant satisfaction of at least 90% per course, per trainer and as a monthly average.
* Complete course content readiness before every delivery.
* Recruitment and replacement within contractual timelines.
* Full local, legal and financial compliance, with no Material Breach events.
* Programme financial performance against budget and forecast, including full revenue recovery.
* Minimal SLA service credits, with Rectification Plans and claims submitted on time.

**Professional Competence**

No day is the same, so it is important that you can prioritise, manage your time successfully, and work both proactively and reactively.

* Strong programme and project management capability across multiple workstreams, markets and stakeholders.
* Proven financial control: budgets, forecasting, revenue recovery, cost-to-invoice reconciliation and commercial risk management.
* Experience managing to contractual SLAs and KPIs, including evidence-based claims and corrective action planning.
* Strong governance, risk and issue management.
* Ability to translate business requirements into practical, measurable programme plans.
* Confident management of senior client stakeholders, including leading formal client and account meetings.
* People leadership: performance management, recruitment and team development.
* Strong analytical and problem-solving skills; able to interpret training data and KPI reports.
* Excellent written and verbal communication and presentation skills.
* High proficiency in Microsoft Office, particularly Excel, PowerPoint and Teams.
* Working knowledge of TMSi or another learning management system is advantageous.

**Personal Competence**

* Demonstrates accountability and ownership for results.
* Professional and confident with senior internal and external stakeholders.
* High emotional intelligence and cultural awareness across diverse markets.
* Commercially minded, with strong attention to detail.
* Proactive in identifying issues and opportunities rather than waiting for direction.
* Calm and decisive under pressure; manages competing priorities effectively.
* Builds trust and credibility with the client, the team and vendors.
* Positive, collaborative and solutions-focused.

Specifically, within Sport Medicine / Performance , technology is core infrastructure rather than a support afterthought: electronic health records, clinical and athlete-monitoring platforms, analytics and cybersecurity must be specified, procured, deployed and integrated to enable safe clinical delivery and evidence-based performance health.
  
  
The role works closely with clinical, operations, finance and enabling teams to translate business and clinical needs into healthcare technology and data requirements, coordinating with function owners and QTech to ensure solutions are aligned with healthcare requirements and that data is usable for decision-making. * Digital Health Strategy & Technology Requirements
* Implement approved QHC Digital Blueprint and define QHC's health technology requirements and digital roadmap across clinical, operational and enabling domains, aligned with the organization's startup priorities and target operating model
* Translate clinical and business needs into technology specifications, architecture principles and a prioritized delivery plan
* Advise leadership on build-versus-leverage decisions across the QIC / QTech and partner ecosystem
* Coordinate with QTech and relevant function owners on interoperability and integration requirements across clinical, operational and administrative systems
* Data Management, Analytics & Business Intelligence
* Define QHC's healthcare data requirements, information flows, data ownership and reporting needs across functions
* Define and coordinate analytics and reporting requirements that support data-driven clinical, operational and leadership decision-making
* Track data availability, quality, ownership and reporting gaps, coordinating with function owners to ensure healthcare data is usable for decision-making
* Support reporting and data needs across the organization as capability matures
* QTech / QIC SLA & Vendor Service Delivery
* Define, establish and manage service-level agreements with QIC / QTech and technology partners, ensuring strong, accountable service delivery to QHC
* Monitor vendor and partner performance against SLAs and drive remediation where service falls short
* Act as the primary QHC coordination point with QTech and relevant technology stakeholders on healthcare-specific technology requirements and delivery priorities
* Cybersecurity, Data Privacy & Governance
* In coordination with QIC, embed cybersecurity, data privacy and information-governance controls across all platforms and data flows from the outset
* In coordination with QIC, ensure compliance with Saudi data-protection and healthcare information regulations and applicable international standards
* In coordination with QIC, establish access controls, audit trails and incident-response readiness for health and personal data
* Deployment, Integration & Readiness
* Oversee deployment and integration readiness for all technology, ensuring systems are tested, secure and operational ahead of go-live milestones
* Coordinate healthcare-specific testing and readiness activities with QTech and relevant clinical and operational teams
* Track technology readiness against the enterprise activation roadmap
* Innovation & Digital Enablement
* Identify and introduce digital health innovations — telehealth, remote athlete monitoring, wearables and AI-assisted tools — aligned with partner best practice
* Pilot and scale digital solutions that enhance clinical quality, athlete outcomes and operational efficiency

**Requirements**
**EXPERIENCE & ACADEMIC QUALIFICATIONS**
Bachelor's degree in Computer Science, Information Systems, Health Informatics, Engineering, or a related field is required. A Master's degree and recognized certifications (e.g. health informatics, cybersecurity, TOGAF, ITIL, or vendor platform certifications
  
  
8+ years of progressive experience in digital health, healthcare IT, health informatics or technology delivery, including experience defining healthcare technology requirements, supporting EHR and healthcare platform delivery, and coordinating technology readiness in new or transforming organizations.
  
  
Demonstrated experience managing technology vendors and SLAs, data management and analytics, and cybersecurity / data-privacy controls within a healthcare environment. Experience within accredited healthcare institutions (JCI, CBAHI) is an advantage.
  
  
Working knowledge of Saudi data-protection and healthcare information regulatory frameworks, and of interoperability and integration across clinical and administrative systems.

Title: Director, Information Technology
Description:
CFS Brands is seeking an experienced
**Director of Information Technology**
to provide operational and people leadership across its global technology environment. Reporting to the Vice President of Information Technology, this role is accountable for IT Operations, End User Services, Network Infrastructure, and Cybersecurity across all facilities and business units. The Director builds capable, independent leaders; establishes consistent service and security standards; and translates business and technology priorities into measurable operational results. The position partners with the VP of IT on planning, budgets, and major decisions and may assume responsibility for additional technology functions as organizational needs evolve.
  
  
**Key Result Areas**

* Lead global IT Operations, including servers, enterprise platforms, storage, backups, disaster recovery, identity and access management, and operational resilience.
* Oversee End User Services and the Helpdesk, establishing service standards, escalation processes, customer experience expectations, and measurable support performance.
* Direct global network infrastructure, connectivity, wireless, site infrastructure, and lifecycle planning across corporate, manufacturing, distribution, and international locations.
* Lead IT security operations, incident-response exercises, vulnerability and audit remediation, third-party security controls, and technology recovery testing against defined recovery objectives. Coordinate business-continuity decisions and enterprise risk acceptance with business owners and VP of IT.
* Partner with the VP of Information Technology to develop and execute multi-year infrastructure, cybersecurity, and IT service roadmaps, translating strategic objectives into operational priorities, resource plans, and measurable outcomes.
* Build, coach, and develop high-performing managers and team leaders who demonstrate ownership, sound judgment, accountability, and independent leadership. Set clear expectations, provide ongoing feedback, address performance gaps, identify emerging talent, and establish succession plans.
* Establish a culture of accountability, operational discipline, and continuous improvement. Translate priorities into actionable plans with named owners, measurable service outcomes, realistic timelines, and regular performance reviews.
* Ensure reliable operations through incident, problem, change, asset, capacity, and configuration management practices; oversee major incident response and service restoration.
* Establish and enforce consistent IT policies, architecture standards, access controls, documentation, and operational processes across global facilities.
* Develop operating and capital budget plans, manage spending and forecasts, and recommend major investments and commitments for VP of IT approval.
* Lead strategic programs, infrastructure modernization, technology integration, and cross-functional initiatives through clear ownership, milestones, performance measures, risk management, and consistent follow-through.
* Exercise sound judgment and independent decision-making within delegated operational, staffing, and financial authority. Recommend capacity and priority tradeoffs; escalate material business risks, enterprise-level priority changes, and significant investment decisions to the VP of IT.
* Manage critical vendors, managed service providers, licensing, contracts, service levels, and supplier performance to maximize value and reduce operational risk.
* Assume leadership responsibility for additional technology functions as assigned, based on evolving organizational needs, business priorities, and departmental structure.

**Education / Experience**

* Bachelor’s degree in Computer Science, Information Systems, Information Technology, or a related field; equivalent relevant experience may be considered.
* Minimum of ten (10) years of progressive experience in enterprise IT, including infrastructure, operations, networks, cybersecurity, or service delivery.
* Minimum of five (5) years of leadership experience, including demonstrated success managing and developing managers, supervisors, or multidisciplinary IT teams.
* Experience supporting geographically distributed operations and managing complex, business-critical technology environments.
* Professional certifications in IT service management, cybersecurity, cloud, networking, or project management are a plus.
* Bilingual proficiency in Spanish is a plus but not required.

**Qualifications Required**
The type of experience required to effectively perform the essential functions and responsibilities of this position are:
  
  

* Demonstrated ability to lead enterprise IT operations and establish global standards across diverse locations and business functions.
* Strong knowledge of server and cloud infrastructure, storage, backup and recovery, identity and access management, and endpoint support.
* Strong understanding of enterprise networking, connectivity, segmentation, remote access, and infrastructure lifecycle management.
* Practical expertise in cybersecurity governance and operations, including incident response, monitoring, vulnerability management, and security risk.
* Ability to establish operational KPIs, service-level expectations, disaster recovery objectives, and continuous improvement programs.
* Demonstrated success developing managers into effective, independent leaders; improving team performance; coaching through performance challenges; establishing accountability; and building leadership succession.
* Experience preparing and managing operating and capital budgets, business cases, forecasts, and vendor negotiations within approved authority.
* Proven ability to prioritize competing initiatives, drive execution through accountable team leaders, resolve obstacles, and communicate progress, risks, and recommendations to organizational leadership.
* Knowledge of ERP, CRM, warehouse management, manufacturing, data, web, and workflow platforms sufficient to partner with or lead assigned functions.
* Excellent written and verbal communication, ability to influence organizational leadership, sound judgment, conflict resolution, and decisive leadership during critical incidents.
* Business acumen, analytical problem-solving skills, and a commitment to service excellence, security, and continuous improvement.

Title: Senior Vice President, Global Services
Description:
****Responsibilities****
The
**Senior Vice President, Global Services**
owns the end-to-end delivery of Octave implementation, deployment, and migration services worldwide. Reporting to the Chief Revenue Officer, this role is accountable for the global portfolio of customer programs, from initial deployments to enterprise cloud consolidations and legacy migrations.
  
  
This role makes services a growth engine, not just a delivery function. You will lead regional delivery, project management, deployment engineering, solution architecture, training, and cutover teams across Americas, EMIA, and APAC while building one global delivery system. The outcome is shorter time-to-value, repeatable deployments, productized services, improved margin and predictability, and greater go-live confidence.
  
  
**Transform and Accelerate Global Services Execution**

* Build one global delivery system. Replace regional variation with a consistent global methodology for project governance, portfolio health, forecasting, risk, and escalation management.
* Stand up a global PMO and center of excellence. Create global delivery and technical implementation capabilities with flexible resourcing and follow-the-sun coverage.
* Shift the operating culture. Move from bespoke customer requirements toward a software-implementation mindset: configure rather than customize, and address product gaps through the roadmap rather than services hours.
* Align services to the revenue motion. Connect Services with Sales, Channel, and Customer Success through services attach, migration offers, clean handoffs, and consistent scoping and estimating.
* Hire, train, and shift talent globally. Bring in modern SaaS delivery expertise, re-skill tenured talent, develop regional successors, and reshape roles for the future operating model.
* Tighten the R&D-to-Services loop. Turn implementation friction into prioritized roadmap input and roadmap delivery into faster, cleaner, more repeatable deployments.

****What You'll Own****

* Global services P&L, utilization and portfolio performance. Own worldwide services revenue, margin, utilization, backlog, forecasting, services attach, conversion, and on-time/on-budget delivery.
* Mission-critical go-lives, worldwide. Own global playbooks, governance, escalation paths, follow-the-sun support, and executive intervention for at-risk deployments.
* Global cloud migration program. Lead migration of Octave's installed base to the cloud, including commercial offers, technical execution, customer change management, data residency, and migration tooling.
* Services transformation. Move from bespoke work toward productized offerings for deployments, cloud transitions, consolidations, and AI enablement, supported by reusable accelerators and reference architectures.
* Partner and delivery ecosystem. Expand and govern the global SI and reseller network with consistent certification, quality standards, and joint-delivery models.
* Regulatory and compliance-aware delivery. Meet applicable security, GDPR, data-sovereignty, and country-specific requirements without fragmenting the global operating model.
* Customer outcomes. Partner with Customer Success, Support, and Product to improve time-to-value, post-go-live stabilization, and customer reference-ability.
* Team. Lead and develop a global organization spanning delivery, program management, architecture, engineering, migration, training, and field readiness, with 1,000+ FTEs plus contractor, nearshore/offshore, and partner capacity.

****Education / Qualifications****

* A senior global services executive with 20+ years of enterprise software delivery experience, including at least 8 years leading services organizations at VP/SVP scale and direct accountability for a $100M+ multi-region services P&L. You have led services teams across at least two of the three major regions (Americas, EMEA, APAC) and understand what it takes to run one global operating model across different labor markets, procurement cultures, and regulatory environments.
* You've done this in a mission-critical, regulated, or 24/7-operations software category — public safety, healthcare, utilities, manufacturing quality, industrial asset management, financial services trading systems, air traffic, defense — somewhere downtime is not an option and customers are operationally dependent on your software the moment it goes live.
* You've led a services transformation at global scale, not just managed delivery. You've taken a custom-project organization and moved it meaningfully toward productized, repeatable, partner-leveraged delivery across multiple regions, and you can speak to the specific levers you pulled and the numbers that moved.
* You've owned a cloud migration program at scale — moving an installed base of on-prem customers to SaaS or managed cloud across multiple countries — and you understand the commercial, technical, change-management, and data-sovereignty mechanics of doing that without breaking customer trust.
* You know how to operate inside a revenue organization. You've partnered tightly with Sales and Channel on attach, packaging, and pricing of services; you treat the forecast as a shared commitment; and you can hold the line on delivery quality and margin while still moving at the speed the revenue engine demands.
* You lead in the field, globally. Customers on every continent expect to meet the executive who is accountable for their deployment. You're comfortable on-site at 2 a.m. during a cutover, in an executive briefing the next week, and in a board review the week after — and you build regional leaders who can carry that presence when you're not in the room.
* You make decisions with incomplete information, hold a clear line on quality and commitments across time zones and cultures, and have a track record of building global organizations people want to stay at.

**Nice to Have**

* Direct experience delivering mission-critical operational software (dispatch, quality management, EAM/APM, or comparable categories)
* Background as a customer-side operations or technology executive who later moved vendor-side
* Experience with Hexagon-heritage platforms or comparable enterprise software ecosystems
* Experience integrating an AI-assisted offering into an established services motion
* Experience operating in-country delivery entities, works-council environments, and public-sector or regulated-industry procurement outside North America
* Additional languages beyond English

****About Octave****
Octave builds mission-critical software for organizations the world depends on — public safety agencies, quality and compliance-driven manufacturers, and asset-intensive industrial operators across energy, utilities, and infrastructure. Our products sit at the heart of our customers' operations: when they go live, downtime is not an option, and customers are operationally dependent on our software from day one.
  
  
Following Octave's spin-off from Hexagon, we are accelerating a global shift to cloud-delivered, AI-enabled solutions. Our installed base of on-premises customers — across dozens of countries, regulatory regimes, and industry standards — needs a confident, well-orchestrated path forward, and new customers on every continent expect faster, more predictable deployments than these industries have historically experienced. This role exists to make that true everywhere Octave operates.
  
  
**Why work for Octave?**
Octave is the rare combination of category-leading products, a customer base that genuinely matters, and a company at an inflection point — fresh out of a spin-off, with the mandate and the runway to modernize how mission-critical software is delivered worldwide. Sitting inside the revenue organization, this seat connects delivery excellence directly to growth. The next few years are when the services model for these industries gets rewritten globally, and the person in this seat gets to do the rewriting — on every continent Octave serves.
  
  
**Everyone is welcome**
At Octave, we believe that diverse and inclusive teams are critical to the success of our people and our business. Here, everyone is welcome. As an inclusive workplace, we don't discriminate. In fact, we embrace differences and are fully committed to creating equal opportunities, an inclusive environment, and fairness for all.

Title: IT Manager
Company: Dave Steel Company, a Walters Group Company
Description:
Since 1929, Dave Steel Company, a Walters Group Company, has primarily focused on industrial projects requiring expert fabrication, exceptional quality, and exemplary service across the United States. As Dave Steel grows and expands into new markets, we are seeking to welcome aspiring and driven individuals to our team who share our vision, mission and core values.

We are incredibly proud of our projects, *to name a few: Sierra Nevada Brewery in Asheville, NC, the Mission Hospital Cancer Center in Asheville, NC, The ASU End Zone in Boone, NC, and the Pratt Whitney Building in Asheville, NC.*

  

We're an AISC Certified Fabricator in business since 1929. We are committed to supporting and developing our teams. We also ensure a positive, safe, collaborative work environment with ample personal and career development opportunities.

If you want to be a part of our team–read on and apply. Even if you feel like you don’t meet all the criteria, please give it a shot, and still apply.

**Role Overview**

The IT Manager is the primary IT resource for Dave Steel, the U.S. division of Walters Group. Reporting to the VP, Digital & Technology at Walters Group, this hands-on position is responsible for day-to-day IT support, infrastructure administration, system reliability, and technical issue resolution across Dave Steel locations.

We are seeking an experienced technical generalist who is comfortable supporting employees, troubleshooting servers and networks, maintaining core infrastructure, responding to outages, and completing technical projects. The successful candidate will take ownership of local issues through resolution while communicating clearly with employees and escalating appropriately when additional expertise is required.

The position operates as part of the broader Walters Digital & Technology organization and works closely with specialists across networking, Microsoft 365, systems administration, cybersecurity, applications, and infrastructure. Walters Group establishes enterprise standards and technical direction, while the IT Manager implements and supports those standards within Dave Steel.

As the Dave Steel IT team grows, this position is expected to provide day-to-day leadership, mentoring, workload prioritization, and technical guidance to local IT support staff. The role does not require extensive formal management experience, but the successful candidate should demonstrate the ability and interest to lead and develop junior technical employees.

**This role is 100% on-site**.

**Key Responsibilities**

IT Support & Service Delivery

* Serve as the primary point of contact for day-to-day IT support at Dave Steel, providing responsive, hands-on assistance to employees and local leaders.
* Troubleshoot and resolve issues involving desktops, laptops, mobile devices, printers, phones, user accounts, applications, connectivity, and plant-floor technology.
* Own support requests through resolution, including communication, documentation, follow-up, and escalation to Walters Group specialists when required.
* Prioritize support activities based on business impact, urgency, and operational requirements.
* Support employee onboarding and offboarding, device deployment, access changes, asset management, and related documentation.
* Create and maintain knowledge articles, technical procedures, and user documentation.

  

Systems & Infrastructure Administration

* Administer, maintain, and troubleshoot Windows Server, Active Directory, VMware, networking, wireless, VPN, and related infrastructure.
* Support Microsoft 365 technologies including Entra ID, Exchange Online, Teams, SharePoint, OneDrive, and Intune within established Walters Group standards.
* Coordinate and perform patching, maintenance, upgrades, equipment replacement, and routine infrastructure changes.
* Support backup, recovery, and disaster recovery procedures, including regular validation and documentation.
* Lead the on-site response to outages and operational technology issues, engaging Walters technical resources as required.

Title: Senior Manager, Wholesale Operations
Description:
**Company Mission:** Rhoback is a community of passionate and motivated people looking to generate positivity, bring people together, and inspire activity by creating high quality products and engaging content for those who seek inspiration, motivation, and connection with a #craveactivity mentality.

**The Role**

The Senior Manager, Wholesale Operations owns day-to-day wholesale order execution, from account onboarding and order capture through allocation execution, fulfillment, delivery, invoicing coordination, and exception resolution. The role partners closely with the Customization Manager, who owns decoration and customization execution across channels.

This is an operating leadership role, not simply order processing. The Senior Manager makes day-to-day decisions within established commercial and inventory priorities, anticipates constraints, resolves issues, and escalates material tradeoffs. Wholesale Sales owns commercial commitments; Planning sets inventory priorities; the Customization Manager owns decoration methods, approvals, production routing, vendor performance, and quality.

**What You’ll Do**

* Own the wholesale order lifecycle: order intake and accuracy, validation, entry, allocation execution, release, shipment, delivery confirmation, and exception resolution. Maintain a reliable order book covering backorders, cancellations, at-risk commitments, and expected shipments; communicate revenue risks to Sales and Finance.
* Lead operational account onboarding and maintain account requirements for EDI, retailer portals, routing guides, labeling, packaging, documentation, and vendor compliance. Track deductions, chargebacks, and service failures; correct root causes and support service standards appropriate to Green Grass, specialty, and key accounts.
* Partner with Planning on availability, reservations, allocation, replenishment, and demand visibility. Execute allocations within approved channel and inventory priorities, identify shortages early, and ensure commitments are accurately represented across systems and fulfillment locations.
* Own wholesale fulfillment coordination with distribution partners, including shipping priorities, account routing requirements, service, cost, and on-time delivery. Partner closely with the Customization Manager on decorated-order handoffs, capacity and production status, inventory readiness, and customer delivery commitments; escalate risks and resolve cross-functional exceptions.
* Lead wholesale account service and Inside Sales, including order acknowledgments, status communication, escalations, workload, coaching, and performance. Coordinate custom-order customer communication with the Customization Manager and Wholesale Sales. Partner with Finance on customer setup, credit holds, terms, invoicing, deductions, and disputes.
* Own wholesale operating processes and data quality across NetSuite, RepSpark, Shopify, EpicStitch, EDI, and related tools. Develop SOPs, training, reporting, system requirements, and practical automation improvements to support scalable growth.
* Maintain a wholesale operations scorecard covering OTIF, fill rate, order accuracy, cycle time, aged backlog, cancellations, and compliance deductions. Lead issue resolution with Sales, Planning, the Customization Manager, Operations, Finance, and external partners; communicate risks early and drive corrective actions.

**What We’re Looking For**

* Working knowledge of wholesale order-to-delivery operations, inventory allocation, fulfillment, EDI, vendor compliance, routing requirements, and deductions; experience with specialty and key/national accounts preferred.
* Ability to manage capacity and delivery commitments, lead teams, and coordinate effectively with Sales, Planning, Finance, distribution, and external sales representatives.
* Strong judgment, analytical ability, organization, and direct communication in a growing business; experience with decorated/customized products and practical automation is a plus.

**What Success Looks Like**

* Accurate, current order-book visibility and dependable shipment commitments.
* Strong on-time/in-full wholesale delivery, fill rate, and order accuracy, with declining aged backlog and avoidable cancellations; clear coordination and early issue escalation for customized orders.
* Fewer routing violations, chargebacks, deductions, and recurring service exceptions.
* Clear account operating standards, effective Inside Sales coverage, and documented, scalable workflows.
* Proactive communication of constraints, decisions, and wholesale shipment risks to leadership.

**Education and Experience**

* 5+ years in wholesale, sales, customer, or supply-chain operations; apparel, footwear, or branded consumer products experience strongly preferred.
* Experience with ERP and B2B order platforms (NetSuite, RepSpark, or comparable), operating KPIs, process improvement, and systems implementation.

**Compensation**

Base salary range: $110,000 - $130,000 per year. Please note that actual salaries will vary based on factors including but not limited to location, experience, and performance. Additional rewards may include performance bonuses, an FTO policy, and many other progressive benefits.

You may be assigned additional duties, activities, or responsibilities to support your professional growth and development within the organization and to meet evolving business needs. Title: Project Manager
Description:
**POSITION SUMMARY**  
We are looking for a hands-on, experienced Senior Project Manager to take ownership of complex, custom-engineered manufacturing projects from kickoff through final customer acceptance. This person will be the main point of contact for the customer and will work closely with engineering, purchasing, manufacturing, assembly, controls, and service to keep projects moving forward. The role involves managing schedules and budgets, coordinating resources, anticipating, and solving problems, and making sure we deliver what we promise.
  
  
This position requires strong mechanical understanding, experience in a manufacturing environment, and the ability to work through challenges as they arise. The successful candidate does not need to be a design engineer, but should understand how machines are designed, built, assembled, tested, and installed. Most importantly, we're looking for someone who takes ownership. This is not simply a project tracking role. We need someone who is comfortable working with customers, walking the manufacturing floor, asking questions, addressing problems, and holding teams accountable to get projects across the finish line.  
  
**ESSENTIAL FUNCTIONS**  
**Project Management**

* Manage multiple custom-engineered projects from initial kickoff through manufacturing, assembly, testing, installation, and final customer acceptance.
* Develop and maintain project schedules, milestones, and key deliverables.
* Coordinate engineering, purchasing, machining, fabrication, assembly, controls, and service activities.
* Monitor progress, identify potential delays, and develop plans to keep projects on track.
* Lead regular project meetings, establish action items, and follow through to completion.
* Keep management informed of project status, risks, resource needs, and potential issues.

  
**Customer Management**

* Serve as the primary contact for customers throughout the project.
* Lead kickoff meetings, design reviews, project updates, and customer milestone meetings.
* Communicate project status, schedule changes, and open issues clearly and professionally.
* Manage customer expectations and address concerns in a timely manner.
* Build strong customer relationships through responsiveness, ownership, and follow-through.

  
**Project Coordination**

* Work closely with engineering to ensure designs meet customer requirements and project expectations.
* Coordinate engineering releases, drawings, bills of material, and purchasing needs to support production schedules.
* Work with manufacturing and assembly teams to address design, production, and equipment-related issues.
* Understand how engineering changes affect cost, schedule, and the overall project.
* Help resolve conflicts involving priorities, resources, and production deadlines.

  
**Testing, Runoff, and Installation**

* Plan and coordinate machine testing and customer runoff activities.
* Ensure project is ready for testing and customer review.
* Work with engineering, assembly, and controls teams to resolve outstanding issues.
* Lead customer runoff meetings and document punch-list items and required corrections.
* Working with Manufacturing Manager, coordinate customer installation, and startup activities, including personnel, schedules, and resources.
* Take ownership of problems that arise during testing, installation, and startup, driving them through resolution.
* Ensure all outstanding items are addressed through final customer acceptance.

  
**Project Costs/Scope and Process Improvement**

* Monitor project costs, budgets, schedules, and contractual requirements.
* Identify customer-requested changes and communicate their impact on cost and timing.
* Ensure project changes are carefully reviewed, documented, and approved.
* Identify potential cost overruns, rework, and other project risks.
* Maintain accurate project schedules, status reports, and documentation.
* Look for ways to improve project planning, communication, and execution.

  
**POSITION REQUIREMENTS**

* Bachelor’s degree in mechanical engineering, manufacturing engineering, engineering technology, project management, or a related field preferred. Equivalent hands-on experience will be considered.
* 5+ years of project management experience in manufacturing, custom machinery, automation, or a similar environment.
* Experience managing complex, custom-engineered equipment, or machinery projects and leading and holding people accountable without direct supervisory authority.
* Strong mechanical aptitude and understanding of machine design, drawings, manufacturing processes, machining, fabrication, and assembly.
* Ability to understand how engineering decisions affect manufacturing, equipment performance, cost, and delivery.
* Experience coordinating machine testing, customer runoff, installation, and startup activities.
* Strong customer communication and problem-solving skills.
* Ability to manage multiple projects and competing priorities.

* Experience with project scheduling tools, ERP/MRP systems, and Microsoft Office.
* Fit UNISIG Core Values: Driven to perform; Solve problems, don’t create them; Strong individual who values a team; Desire to find what’s next; Committed to detail and consistency.

  
**PHYSICAL REQUIREMENTS/WORKING CONDITIONS**

* Primarily works in an office environment, with regular time spent on the manufacturing floor.
* Regularly operates a computer and standard office equipment.

 **Job Description**

**The Opportunity:**

As the Manager, Operations Learning, you will build the learning strategy, programs and capability solutions that help Maple Leaf Foods’ Operations teams operate safely, consistently and with excellence. Reporting to the Director, Talent Development & DEI, you’ll be a key partner to plant leadership, Operations, Health & Safety, Operational Excellence, FSQA, Supply Chain, Engineering and Asset Reliability, translating enterprise transformation priorities into practical learning, tools, routines and behaviour change across the manufacturing network.

Core to the role is turning strategy into executable learning plans. You’ll work closely with plants to understand day-to-day realities and equip leaders, supervisors, trainers and team members to execute safely and consistently. You’ll design blended learning, enable facilitators and trainers, leverage learning technology and data, and measure impact on capability, adoption and business outcomes.  
  
Any MLF team member interested in being considered for this role are encouraged to apply online by November 30. Applications received beyond that date are not guaranteed consideration.  
  
Reason for vacancy: Existing Headcount  
Compensation: $96,000 - $141,000 CAD base pay annually plus annual short-term incentive  
  
The above compensation reflects the target compensation for the position at the time of posting. The base salary offered may vary based on a variety of factors including skills, experience, education, training, job- related knowledge, and other organizational requirements. For part-time roles, salaries are adjusted according to scheduled hours. In addition to base salary, this role is eligible to participate in Maple Leaf’s annual short-term incentive plan.  
  
**Snapshot of a Day-in-the-Life:**

* **Partner to Identify Capability Gaps:** Partner with Operations leaders, Plant Managers, HRBPs and functional teams (FSQA, Health & Safety, Operational Excellence, Engineering) to identify capability gaps and translate business priorities into practical learning strategies.
* **Design Blended Learning:** Design and develop practical, role-relevant, blended learning (classroom, virtual, digital, on-the-job), including facilitator guides, job aids and assessments. Partner with SMEs to turn technical content into clear learning experiences.
* **Strengthen Onboarding and Talent Development:** Strengthen onboarding, job-specific, cross-training and qualification pathways to accelerate time-to-productivity and improve consistency across sites.
* **Build the Leadership Pipeline:** Design and execute an Operations Leadership Accelerator program that builds frontline and operations leadership capability and grows Maple Leaf Foods’ internal leadership pipeline.
* **Reinforce Safety and Operational Excellence:** Build learning and tools that reinforce safety expectations and leader accountability (Safety Promise, Zero Hero) and bring Operational Excellence priorities to plant teams.
* **Deliver and Coach:** Deliver programs and coach internal facilitators, trainers, supervisors and plant leaders to make new ways of working part of everyday routines and coaching conversations.
* **Measure and Improve:** Evaluate and improve programs using people and learning data, feedback and operational results.
* **Manage Learning Systems and Vendors:** Manage learning systems, digital tools and external vendors to keep content current and scalable.
* **Build Trusted Relationships:** Build trusted relationships across plants and functions, influence without authority, and travel to sites as required to support delivery.

 **Qualifications**

**What You’ll Bring:**

* **Proven Leadership in Learning:** Proven and recurring success at the Manager level leading learning and development, organizational development or change enablement, ideally supporting manufacturing, food processing, CPG or a similarly complex frontline environment.
* **Learning Expertise:** Strong knowledge of adult learning, instructional design, facilitation, evaluation and behaviour change, with the ability to build programs for onboarding, technical capability, safety culture and frontline leadership.
* **Manufacturing Acumen:** Understanding of manufacturing environments, including safety, quality, standard work and plant performance. Lean, Operational Excellence or continuous improvement experience is an asset.
* **Translating Strategy into Learning:** Ability to translate strategy, operational requirements and technical content into practical learning, with strong facilitation and communication skills that engage operational audiences.
* **Stakeholder Management and Influence:** Strong stakeholder management, consulting and influencing skills across levels.
* **Project Management:** Strong project management skills to manage multiple priorities and vendors in a fast-paced environment.
* **Data-Driven Change Leadership:** Curious change leader who is comfortable working with technologies (LMS/LXP, Microsoft 365, analytics) and using data to drive decisions.

 **Additional Information**

**What We Offer at Maple Leaf Foods:**

* Being part of a high-performance, people-focused company that has an inspiring and unique vision to become the most sustainable protein company on earth, and a deep commitment to sustainable protein across North America.
* An inclusive company culture and a work environment that keeps our people safe, rewards excellence, and empowers everyone to learn and contribute their best.

* Defined Contribution Pension Plan with company matching that starts on your first day of employment.
* Learning and development opportunities, including workshops, ‘speaker series’ events, and resources that allow you to develop your skills and progress your career.
* Comprehensive tuition reimbursement program that supports continuous learning and development of our team members through investment in eligible degrees, diplomas, professional certification, or trades programs.

Title: Program Director
Description:
**SUMMARY**

Haven House, a program of Recovery Network of Programs, Inc. (RNP), is a twelve-bed, DPH-licensed and CARF-accredited Clinically Managed High-Intensity Residential Treatment program (ASAM Level 3.5) for cisgender and transgender women. The program provides trauma-informed, gender-specific treatment and recovery support for women with substance use disorders and co-occurring mental health disorders in a structured environment staffed 24 hours a day.

In accordance with RNP’s Mission Statement, Philosophy of Client Care, and Code of Ethics as stated in the Personnel Policies, the Program Director leads Haven House’s clinical and residential operations. The director oversees staffing, service delivery, quality improvement, and regulatory compliance so residents receive coordinated care and can transition to the next appropriate level of care.

**SPECIFIC DUTIES AND RESPONSIBILITIES**  
All duties are subject to accommodation in accordance with the Americans with Disabilities Act (ADA).

* Oversee program operations and compliance with ASAM Level 3.5 criteria, applicable Connecticut Medicaid 1115 Demonstration requirements, DPH regulations, DMHAS contractual requirements, CARF standards, DDCAT-E principles, and agency policies.
* Build a supportive work environment and promote collaboration across disciplines.
* Maintain a safe therapeutic environment through oversight of residential operations, client safety, infection prevention, and emergency preparedness.
* Direct clinical, residential, and operational workflows to keep day-to-day services coordinated.
* Lead, supervise, and evaluate assigned staff. Coordinate clinical oversight and required supervision with the designated Clinical Supervisor and ensure staff deliver integrated, trauma-informed, gender-responsive services.
* Use integrated care, team building, crisis management, and risk assessment to guide program operations and staff development.
* Monitor census, referrals, occupancy, and access to care. Work with referral sources to support appropriate program utilization.
* Ensure the staffing plan provides safe 24-hour residential coverage, meets applicable discipline-specific coverage requirements, and supports staff training, competency, and supervision.
* Oversee admission, continued stay, transfer, and discharge processes with qualified clinical staff to ensure decisions reflect ASAM criteria and individual treatment needs.
* Monitor weekly clinical and recovery programming against Level 3.5 requirements, including 20 total hours of programming, at least 10 hours of clinical treatment, and at least one hour of individual or family therapy within those clinical hours.
* Lead projects that improve program operations and service delivery.
* Prepare and submit required reports on time.
* Assist with budget preparation and monitor revenues and expenditures.
* Participate in long-range planning, quality improvement, and quality assurance.
* Oversee incident reporting, risk management, and corrective action follow-up.
* Serve as a liaison and educator to community and professional organizations.
* Represent RNP at statewide meetings on co-occurring disorders.
* Provide assigned clinical on-call oversight and ensure staff know how to access designated on-call support.
* Track quality indicators, audit findings, utilization, resident outcomes, and satisfaction. Develop corrective action plans as indicated.
* Oversee the accuracy, timeliness, and completeness of client records and required Carelon documentation, consistent with agency, regulatory, and contractual requirements.
* Assumes all other appropriate duties as deemed necessary by the supervisor.
* **SKILLS/ABILITIES**
* Valid Connecticut driver's license may be required.
* Thorough knowledge of human services as provided by community-based, non-profit service organizations.
* Knowledge of and ability to apply management principles and techniques.
* Considerable ability to assess, plan, organize and direct all aspects of program activities.
* Ability to identify and implement program enhancements.
* Ability to prepare comprehensive reports.
* Proven interpersonal skills and supervisory ability.
* Considerable knowledge of federal and state laws and regulations regarding client confidentiality.
* Ability to establish and maintain cooperative professional relationships and project a professional image.
* Excellent oral and written communication skills.
* **EDUCATION AND/OR EXPERIENCE**
* Master’s degree from an accredited college or university in social work, marriage and family therapy, counseling, psychology, or a related field.
* LCSW, LPC, or LMFT license required.
* At least four (4) years of supervisory experience preferred.
* Extensive experience in the provision and supervision of integrated co-occurring treatment.
* **PHYSICAL REQUIREMENT AND WORK ENVIRONMENT**

  The physical requirements and work environment described below are representative of those that an employee must meet to successfully perform the essential functions of this position. Title: Operations Manager
Description:
**Operations Manager and Production and Materials Planner**

We are seeking a hands-on Operations Manager to oversee the day-to-day assembly, inventory, and materials planning activities of our small manufacturing operation.

This individual will be responsible for ensuring that all customer orders are assembled, tested, and shipped on schedule, with the necessary materials, components, and resources available to meet committed delivery dates.

The position directly manages a small team of four assembly employees and one warehouse employee and works closely with our buyer, sales, customer service, and other company departments.

The ideal candidate has practical experience in a manufacturing environment, understands MRP systems (Epicor experience a plus) and material requirements planning, and is comfortable working directly with employees to solve day-to-day operational problems.

This is a working management position requiring both planning and hands-on execution.

**Key Responsibilities**

**1. Production and Assembly Management**

* Supervise and coordinate the daily activities of four assembly employees.
* Develop and maintain assembly schedules based on customer orders, material availability, and delivery commitments.
* Assign work, monitor production progress, and resolve operational issues.
* Ensure assembly work is completed efficiently and meets company quality standards.
* Identify opportunities to improve assembly processes, productivity, and workflow.
* Monitor production capacity and adjust schedules as required.

**2. MRP System and Production Planning**

* Take responsibility for the daily operation and accuracy of the company's MRP system.
* Review customer orders, bills of materials, inventory levels, and material requirements.
* Run MRP planning processes and review purchasing and production recommendations.
* Identify shortages, incorrect inventory records, and potential supply problems.
* Maintain accurate manufacturing schedules and material requirements.
* Work with the appropriate departments to maintain accurate MRP data, including lead times, bills of materials, and inventory parameters.

**3. Purchasing and Supplier Coordination**

* Review MRP purchasing recommendations and direct the buyer regarding materials and components that need to be ordered.
* Establish purchasing priorities based on customer delivery requirements.
* Monitor open purchase orders and supplier delivery commitments.
* Work with the buyer to expedite late or critical components.
* Identify supplier-related risks that could affect manufacturing schedules.
* Help improve supplier delivery reliability and reduce unnecessary inventory.

**4. Inventory and Warehouse Management**

* Supervise the warehouse employee responsible for receiving, stocking, picking, and shipping materials.
* Maintain accurate inventory records and appropriate inventory levels.
* Coordinate cycle counting and investigation of inventory discrepancies.
* Ensure components are available and correctly allocated to production orders.
* Monitor slow-moving and obsolete inventory.
* Improve inventory accuracy, material flow, and warehouse organization.

**5. Customer Order and Delivery Management**

* Review open customer orders and committed delivery dates.
* Ensure required materials and production capacity are available to meet delivery commitments.
* Identify potential delays early and develop corrective action plans.
* Coordinate with sales and customer service regarding order status and delivery risks.
* Provide reliable information on production schedules and expected shipment dates.
* Help ensure products ship complete, correctly, and on time.

**6. Operational Improvement and Reporting**

* Monitor key operational performance indicators, including on-time delivery, inventory accuracy, supplier delivery, and production performance.
* Identify opportunities to improve inventory turnover, reduce shortages, and increase assembly productivity.
* Participate in continuous improvement activities.
* Provide regular operational updates to the General Manager.
* Support the development of effective manufacturing and inventory management procedures.

**Required Qualifications**

* 3–6 years of relevant experience in manufacturing operations, production planning, materials management, or inventory control.
* At least 1 year of experience supervising employees or coordinating the work of a manufacturing team.
* Practical experience using an ERP/MRP system in a manufacturing environment.
* Good understanding of bills of materials, inventory transactions, purchasing requirements, production orders, and supplier lead times.
* Experience coordinating purchasing and production schedules to meet customer delivery requirements.
* Strong organizational, problem-solving, and communication skills.
* Good working knowledge of Microsoft Excel.
* Ability to work independently and manage multiple operational priorities.
* Comfortable working in a small company where the manager is directly involved in day-to-day activities.

**Preferred Qualifications**

* Associate's or bachelor's degree in Operations Management, Supply Chain Management, Business, Engineering, or a related discipline.
* Experience in precision instruments, electromechanical assembly, scientific equipment, or other low-volume manufacturing environments.
* Mechanical knowledge and facility management experience are helpful
* Experience with low-volume, high-mix manufacturing.
* Knowledge of inventory optimization, cycle counting, and production scheduling.
* Familiarity with lean manufacturing and continuous improvement.
* Experience supporting engineering changes and new product introductions.

**Personal Characteristics**

We are looking for someone who is:

* Highly organized and detail-oriented.
* Proactive in identifying material shortages and delivery risks.
* Comfortable supervising a small team.
* Practical, hands-on, and willing to help wherever needed.
* Able to prioritize customer requirements and operational problems.
* Confident using MRP data to make purchasing and scheduling decisions.
* Capable of working with limited day-to-day supervision.
* Interested in growing into a more senior operations management position.

**Performance Expectations**

Success in this role will be measured by:

* Consistently meeting customer delivery commitments.
* Ensuring materials are available when required for assembly.
* Maintaining accurate inventory and MRP records.
* Keeping production schedules organized and current.
* Improving purchasing coordination and supplier delivery performance.
* Maintaining an efficient and well-managed assembly and warehouse operation.
* Identifying and implementing practical operating improvements.

**Responsibilities**

* Lead production planning, scheduling, and manufacturing management; monitor execution and address constraints.
* Use SAP and other enterprise resource planning (ERP) systems, including material requirements planning (MRP), to coordinate materials and production data.
* Apply Microsoft Excel and Excel data analysis to review supply chain analytics, inventory, and operational performance.
* Drive continuous improvement, process improvement, and quality control using Lean manufacturing, Lean management, and Six Sigma methods.
* Provide team leadership and cross-functional communication with production, materials, and supply chain partners.

Title: Vice President, Operations & Client Delivery
Description:

Physicians Revenue Group, Inc. and its family of commonly held companies serve physician and dental

practices across the United States. Our business units provide medical billing and revenue cycle

management, dental revenue cycle management, value-based care programs, digital marketing agency

services, healthcare cybersecurity, and healthcare technology, supported by teams in the United States

and abroad.

**About the role**

This role leads service delivery and client success across our family of companies, which provide revenue

cycle management, dental revenue cycle, and value-based care services to physician and dental

practices nationwide, delivered by onshore and offshore teams.

You will bring delivery and client success together under one standard: every client gets consistent

service, every leader runs to a scorecard, and every team knows what good looks like. This role is for a

healthcare operator who has led directors, held them accountable, and grown client retention at scale.

**Core responsibilities**

**I. Enterprise operations leadership**

* Lead the directors responsible for revenue cycle, dental, and value-based care operations, and the  offshore delivery leadership supporting them.
* Set one operating standard across business units: decision rights, escalation paths, scorecards, and review cadence.
* Coach, develop, and hold directors accountable; address underperformance promptly and fairly.

**II. Client delivery and retention**

* Own client retention and satisfaction outcomes across business units.
* Ensure account transitions, manager changes, and onboarding happen without service disruption.
* Run quarterly client performance reviews on verified data.

**III. Offshore and hybrid delivery**

* Align onshore client success with offshore delivery teams on staffing, quality, productivity, and escalation.
* Set service levels and quality standards that apply equally to onshore and offshore teams.

**IV. Quality, compliance, and controls**

* Partner with the compliance function so delivery meets payer and regulatory requirements, and act on audit findings promptly.
* Ensure documented SOPs, version control, and training are in place for every service line.

**V. Commercial partnership**

* Work alongside the commercial teams as the operational and technical leader, joining client presentations and high-level client discussions where needed.
* Partner with sales and business development on scoping, pricing inputs, and implementation readiness.

**VI. Growth and new service lines**

* Build delivery models for new DSO and MSO services and support new client implementations.

**VII. Financial performance**

* Own delivery cost, margin, and productivity targets for each business unit.
* Use operating data to set staffing plans and improve unit economics.

**90-day priorities**

* **Day 1-30:**
  Meet directors, key clients, and offshore leadership. Review scorecards, retention data, and open issues.
* **Day 31-60:**

**12-month success metrics**

* Client retention at or above target in every business unit.
* Every director on a scorecard, reviewed monthly, with clear actions on underperformance.
* Delivery margin and productivity targets met.

* 12+ years in healthcare operations, including at least 5 years leading directors or multi-site

* Track record of improving client retention and operating margin.

**Preferred**

* Client success leadership experience, especially in healthcare. Highly preferred, though strong,
* transferable operations and client delivery experience will also be considered.
* Value-based care, care management, or dental revenue cycle experience.
* Experience with DSO or MSO operations.
* MBA or MHA.

**Performance framework**

* Quarterly review against retention, quality and compliance, margin, and leadership development.
* Bonus tied to quality, retention, and margin KPIs, not to billing volume.

This role is the senior operating leader for service delivery and is positioned for expanded executive

responsibility as the organization scales.

As part of our leadership team, this role may support initiatives across other business units as the

organization grows.

Location: On-site (Downers Grove, IL)

Compensation: $165,000 - 185,000 + up to 15% annual bonus

Benefits: Health insurance, 401(k) with employer match, paid time off, and professional

development support.

Title: Jr. Operations Manager
Description:
**About ESOTERIC**

ESOTERIC is an automotive studio known internationally for detailing, paint protection film, window tint, and our own car care products. We work on more supercars than anyone else in the Midwest, so we know what it takes to hand a client back their car exactly the way they expected it.

We run the studio on four values: **Integrity, Craftsmanship, Ownership Mentality, and a Relentless Pursuit of Quality.** We hold each other to them, and we invest in people who want to build a long career here.

Our Cleveland team is growing. If you like structure, high standards, and a team that takes its work seriously but not itself, read on.

**The role**

You’ll run day-to-day service operations at our Cleveland studio. That means keeping the schedule tight and our processes consistent, making the numbers visible, and making sure every client gets a professional experience from drop-off to delivery.

This is a hands-on role. The systems are already in place. Your job is to run them well, hold the standard, and report what’s working and what isn’t. You’ll work closely with our department leads and senior leadership. If you do it well, it leads straight to senior operations leadership.

**What you’ll own**

* **The schedule.** The master service schedule across PPF, Window Tint, Detail, and Mechanical. You’ll build it ahead, check it weekly for accuracy and capacity, and sort out the daily conflicts before they turn into a late car.
* **The numbers.** Weekly KPI reporting: projections vs. actuals, labor utilization, damage and claim costs, and comebacks. Share them with the department leads and raise trends, risks, and gaps early, not after the fact.
* **Client escalations.** When something goes sideways, you’re the first call. Handle it professionally and quickly, and bring in department leads when it needs them.
* **Vendors and parts.** All service-related vendor communication, plus coordinating parts with our mechanic.
* **The team.** Give department leads structure and clear direction, and help keep the studio calm, disciplined, and true to our values.

**What you bring**

* 2+ years in service operations, ideally premium automotive or another high-touch service business
* You communicate clearly and coach well, and you’ve built teams that perform
* You’re comfortable with scheduling, gross profit tracking, labor efficiency, and customer metrics
* You care about the client experience as much as the team’s results
* You like a fast pace and high standards (both are on the menu daily)

**Reporting and growth**

You’ll report to the Service Operations Manager. You’ll work closely with department leads, front desk sales, technicians, and accounting. We do performance reviews every quarter and a compensation review once a year.
